_comment: Which model runs which phase, by tier — the one place to turn. Read by scripts/process/dispatch.py; measured by process_kpis.py models (telemetry module). Phases: brainstorm, plan, execute, review. Brainstorm requires tier >= 2 and owner approval before starting plan. A tier without an entry falls back to `default` per phase. `command` is the project's way to start a worker session (the default is Claude Code's CLI; with another harness, put its CLI here): {model} and {prompt} are substituted inside the argv this template splits into; the prompt is one argv element; {branch} and {issue} name the session where the harness labels sessions (Claude Code: `--remote-control={branch}` makes each worker visible in the Claude app — the `=` form, because the flag's optional name would otherwise eat the prompt). TRUST: this command runs on the machine that runs dispatch — a change here is a change to what the steward's host executes; review it like CI configuration. A cell is a model id or `{"model": "...", "effort": "minimal|low|medium|high|xhigh|max", "command": "..."}`: {effort} is substituted like {model}, an argv element carrying it is dropped for a cell without effort (the harness default applies), and an effort its command cannot carry is refused, never ignored; a cell's own `command` (with {model} and {prompt}) wins over `phases.<phase>.command` and `command`, runner and host stay the phase's — e.g. a Tier 3 review on another family in the local file: `{"model": "<codex model>", "effort": "xhigh", "command": "codex exec --model {model} -c model_reasoning_effort={effort} --sandbox read-only {prompt}"}` (a second family makes the review attestation `cross-model`; the default Opus review is `single-family`; such a cell runs unsupervised — for Codex workers and Codex reviews that attest end to end use the variant `model-policy.codex.json` with `--harness codex`). A command file's `model:`/`effort:` frontmatter would override the cell: dispatch refuses it. `env`: environment for worker sessions only, top-level and per phase (`phases.<phase>.env` wins) — e.g. `{"CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL": "sonnet"}` runs built-in subagents on a cheaper model (not a plan reviewer below the plan session's class: attest.py refuses it, `review_evidence`); a worker-only advisor goes into `command` (Claude Code: `--settings '{"advisorModel":"opus"}'`); the owner's own sessions keep their settings; `PROCESS_*` is dispatch's own. `max_workers` caps concurrent dispatched sessions on this host (a session whose phase is over by its own final report holds no slot). `worker_nice` (default 10, 0 = off): local workers start under `nice`, so the merge train keeps its CPU. `stale_minutes` (default 60, a positive integer): a worker with no commit and no report for this long is stale — the tower's `stale-worker` finding, and `tower.py --wait --states …,stale` wakes the steward on a live session that silent (`docs/process/tower.md`).`decision_channel`: how a worker reaches the steward live (e.g. `SendMessage to 'steward'`); the start prompt names it, so the steward's instructions there are not refused as a stranger's; {branch} and {issue} in it are filled as in `command` — default: none, reports and plan decisions carry communication; when set, report lifecycle and blocking events there too. `say_prompt`: a regex for the harness input line `dispatch.py say` checks (group 1 = what is still typed; default: a `>` prompt, maybe boxed). `runner`: `detached` (headless; a `-p` session needs its tool permissions granted in the project's settings or via --permission-mode, else it stops at the first gate) or `tmux` (each worker a window of tmux session `tmux_session` — interactive, a human can open it and `dispatch.py say` can type into it; use a non -p command then, e.g. `claude --model {model} --effort={effort} --permission-mode acceptEdits {prompt}`; a fresh worktree may show a trust dialog on first start). `phases`: per-phase overrides — `{"review": {"command": "...", "runner": "detached", "remote": true}}`; `remote: true` means the session runs on another host (with `"runner": "tmux"` the hand-over command runs in a tmux window — for starters that need a terminal; `list` then shows a failed hand-over as HAND-OVER FAILED); `handover_id`: a regex that captures the other host's session id from what the hand-over printed (group 1; default: the first URL), shown by list, log and the tower (a cloud session, another machine): dispatch creates no worktree here, the command is the hand-over (it must exit 0 once the session is started; its stdout is kept), the branch must be on origin, and the worker reports with `--sync` so `tower.py --remote` sees it. Reviews are the natural remote phase: git-only, CPU-heavy, and a fresh clone on another host is independence for free. `transcripts`: a glob of the harness's session transcripts (JSONL), `{worktree}` substituted with each dispatched worktree of the issue — harness-specific, default none; `finish.py` and `process_kpis.py cost --issue N` sum their `output_tokens`, and say `not measured` without it. `classes`: a model per task class and phase (`[mechanical]`, `[design]` on a task line; unmarked is `standard`, which takes the tier) — consulted before the tier, at every tier (a `[mechanical]` task in Tier 3 runs on its class's model on purpose); `dispatch.py policy --class C` prints the row. A subagent spawn that names its model wins over the harness default; `classes` is where that name comes from (`docs/process/tower.md`). `worker_shell_form` (a string; absent: the template's block `dispatch.SHELL_FORM`): the shell-form paragraph every worker prompt of this policy ends with — one simple command per Bash call, no shell expansions, files through Write/Edit — so the permission allowlist can match each command; your own string replaces it (to extend it, copy the template's wording into yours), `""` drops it; the Codex variant ignores the key (its own sandbox). PROJECT CHOICES go into `docs/process/model-policy.local.json`, laid over this file mapping by mapping (`{"tiers": {"3": {"execute": "..."}}}` changes one cell): this file stays the template's, so a release's edits here still arrive.

review_evidence._comment: What attest.py asks of a Tier 2+ pass (scripts/process/attest_evidence.py), read at the reviewed base: a branch's own edit here does not judge its own pass. cross_model_from_tier: from this tier on a code-review pass carries `cross-model`, or `single-family` plus a committed `skipped cross-model work=<id>: <reason>` (4: never). ranks: model-id prefix -> class rank; a plan-review pass is refused when its model ranks below the plan session's (the newest `planned` report, else the plan's `plan-session model: <id>` line), and every model a cell here names must match one. families: prefixes of other model families, never ranked against these and never smaller. The longest matching prefix decides; an id no prefix matches is unknown and refused. own_family_from_tier: from this tier on only a pass by this project's own family (a ranked model, or the bare family name /review records, e.g. `claude`) clears a plan and proves its code current (check_review, finish.py, the train) — another family's pass stays valid but clears nothing alone (4: never; a project whose second family attests but must not decide alone sets 3). python_files, python_classes: what pytest collects here (its own defaults; name yours if pytest is configured otherwise). test_files: which files of other languages are tests (fnmatch on the repository path, `*` spans folders) — a test a review report names must stand in one, so a Markdown file or a helper module proves no criterion; add a project's own layout (e.g. inline Rust tests in `src/*.rs`). required_records: what a work owes as a record (scripts/process/required_records.py) — a REFUTE for gate code and from Tier 3, a ROOT-CAUSE line after three fix commits on one file, per blocked code round the branch adds a class test (`ROOT-CAUSE … — sites: … — <path>::<test>`, or `sites: none — <reason>`) and from the second such round a `REPLAN work=<id> round=<r>: increment|rebuild — <why>` per follow-up block in the plan, an owner DECISION behind `review-waived:`; a `when` value of an int fact is a threshold (at least); attest refuses without the record or a reasoned `skipped <kind> work=<id>: <reason>` (the owner's word cannot be skipped), and a project appends its own rows under required_records_extra. A project lays its own values over these in model-policy.local.json (`{"review_evidence": {"cross_model_from_tier": 2}}`).
